title: cookwright.json
description: What a repo tells cookwright about itself: its state homes, its agent hosts, its gate. Lives at the repo root.

version.description: Config format version. Bumped only with a migration.

level.description: The level this repo declares. doctor measures it: a piece the level requires that is missing is drift.

hosts.description: Agent hosts this repo is set up for, each once. The first is the default host: the one whose workflow scripts and rules files the CLI names.

baseBranch.description: The branch bundles branch from and merge back into.

paths.description: The state homes and code docs, relative to the repo root. No two of these paths may be equal or nest inside one another.

bundles.description: Directory of bundle state, written only by the bundle CLI. Root-relative, no trailing slash.

closeouts.description: Directory of closeouts, one past-tense file per shipped bundle. Root-relative, no trailing slash.

backlog.description: The backlog file: bugs and enhancements outside the current bundle. Root-relative, no trailing slash.

playbook.description: The bundle playbook every session reads. Root-relative, no trailing slash.

changelog.description: The changelog: generated from release tags by `npx cookwright changelog`, never edited by hand. Root-relative, no trailing slash.

gate.description: The checks that run between bundle phases.

checks.description: Run in order; every one runs even after a failure. A check whose `needs` are not on PATH is skipped and reported, never failed.

run.description: A shell command, as in a package.json script.

needs.description: Executables that must be on PATH for this check to run.

flakes.description: The retry allowlist: a failed gate may be re-run once when the only failures are a named flake. Keys are your backlog ids.

hooks.description: The git hooks `npx cookwright init` installs (.githooks/). Their checks are skipped per commit with COOKWRIGHT_SKIP=<check,…>, never turned off here.

docSync.description: Doc-sync rules the pre-commit hook enforces: when a staged path matches a rule's `code`, a path matching its `docs` must be staged in the same commit. Every rule is checked, so one commit shows every miss.

name.description: Named in the hook's output; each name once.

code.description: Git pathspecs, matched against the staged files by `git diff --cached`: `*` crosses `/`, `:!x` or `:(exclude)x` excludes, `:(glob)x` turns on glob rules. Long magic words are git's own (top, literal, icase, glob, attr, exclude).

docs.description: Git pathspecs: one staged match satisfies the rule. Same pathspec rules as `code`.

ci.description: When present, the landing check asks GitHub (through `gh`) whether this workflow is green on HEAD.
